summary.text: SAME is a low-gravity smoke investigation that aims to quantify smoke particulate sizes and relate droplet size distribution to smoke generation and transport conditions, with implications for smoke detector response.

fuels.text: Smoke generated by overheated spacecraft materials.

geometry.text: Near field hardware installed in the Glovebox with a Far Field Box attached.

gravity.text: Low gravity compared with normal gravity smoke behavior.

measurements.text: Two smoke detectors; particulate on thermophoretic probes analyzed after flight by Transmission Electron microscope (TEM) for primary and aggregate particle dimensions.

claims.text: The investigation aimed to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity.
The investigation planned to develop a numerical code to predict smoke droplet growth as a function of the fuel pyrolysis rate.
The investigation hypothesized that liquid aerosol smokes produced in microgravity will exhibit substantially larger droplet sizes than under the same conditions in normal gravity.
The investigation hypothesized that the change in size distribution and number density will affect smoke detector response, possibly with some detectors not producing an alarm.
The source states that SAME is intended to provide quantitative data on the sensitivity of smoke detectors to reduced gravity smokes.

limitations.text: This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.

modeling_resources.description: Experimental table and analyzed data files from the reduced gravity runs could support future modeling of smoke particle growth. No model is claimed to exist or be validated.
